data.hypothesis: For n in [2,128], the existing route performs one reduction launch and then a device-to-device copy. A single 128-thread CTA can handle these sizes with bounded loads and write directly to out, potentially saving the copy. Preserve n=1's no-kernel copy path because adding a kernel may be slower, and retain the existing hierarchical path above the generic one-CTA capacity.

memory_lessons.applicability: Baseline reference for evaluating this small-input direct-output candidate; it does not establish candidate performance.
memory_lessons.claim: The baseline was valid on all 10 recorded size/seed cases and had three repeated timings with a 46.67 microsecond mean. No candidate timing or alternative program was recorded in the catalog.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Run the candidate through every correctness case and compare its repeated timings with the baseline, including the unchanged n=1 copy route.

data.notes: This is a generic threshold at reduce0's 128-element single-CTA capacity, not a branch on benchmark sizes. The supplied baseline is valid across its 10 cases with three timing samples (mean 46.67 microseconds); the catalog has no prior T2 candidates or source diversity, so there is no measured crossover yet. Candidate correctness and repeated timings remain for the controller to evaluate; no speedup is claimed.
transformations: For 2 <= n <= 128, launch one 128-thread reduce0 CTA that writes its result directly to out, eliminating the intermediate output and final device copy.
Leave the n=1 asynchronous device-to-device copy path and the existing hierarchical reduction fallback for larger sizes unchanged.
